# commutator subgroup　`def.commutator-subgroup`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=def.commutator-subgroup)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.commutator-subgroup.md)

[G,G] is normal, and the quotient $G/[G,G]$ is abelian. More strongly, if $N \trianglelefteq G$ is such that $G/N$ is abelian, then $[G,G] \subseteq N$; hence $G/[G,G]$ is the **maximal abelian quotient** of $G$.

## Notes · **draft**
⭐ Commutators themselves are not associative: in general $[[x,y],z] \ne [x,[y,z]]$; the subgroup they generate is the useful object.

⭐ Examples: $[S_n, S_n] = A_n$; $[G, G] = \{e\}$ if and only if $G$ is abelian.
